items.question: For OE62 molecule JIMHOC (the same geometry already used in QNP008), using the attached geometry and the official PBE+vdW(vacuum) and PBE0(vacuum) orbital-energy lists, identify the HOMO and LUMO at each level and compute both HOMO-LUMO gaps. Report both gaps in eV to four decimal places, state the signed difference (PBE0 gap minus PBE gap), and explain whether this single molecule alone establishes a general relationship between the two functionals.
items.model_input:
The attachment is the JIMHOC XYZ geometry (S0002), 57 atoms. Coordinates are in angstrom (1 nm = 10 angstrom). Atom rows are numbered starting at 1, immediately after the two header lines. This is a single relaxed molecular geometry, not a periodic cell. Occupied orbital energies are listed in ascending order; the HOMO is the last (highest) value in the occupied list. Unoccupied orbital energies are also listed in ascending order; the LUMO is the first (lowest) value in the unoccupied list. The HOMO-LUMO gap is LUMO minus HOMO, in eV.

PBE+vdW(vacuum) occupied energies (eV): -4.196 is the HOMO (last value of the full list). PBE+vdW(vacuum) unoccupied energies (eV): -0.6203700000000001 is the LUMO (first value of the full list). PBE0(vacuum) occupied energies (eV): -5.2578700000000005 is the HOMO (last value). PBE0(vacuum) unoccupied energies (eV): 0.038560000000000004 is the LUMO (first value).

answer_refs.quote: Table 2 column 6 (energies_occ_pbe, unit eV, method PBE+vdW vacuum) description quote: List of eigenvalues of occupied molecular Kohn-Sham orbitals. Given in ascending order, the last value is the HOMO energy.

Table 2 column 14 (energies_unocc_pbe, unit eV, method PBE+vdW vacuum) description quote: List of eigenvalues of virtual (unoccupied) molecular Kohn-Sham orbitals. Given in ascending order, the first value is the LUMO energy. Only virtual states below the vacuum level (i.e. with negative eigenvalue) are listed. If the LUMO energy is positive, only the LUMO energy is listed.

items.rubric: 5 points: PBE gap within 0.0001 eV (1); PBE0 gap within 0.0001 eV (1); correct signed difference within 0.0001 eV (1); correctly states the PBE0 gap is larger (1); explicitly states this single molecule does not establish a general PBE-vs-PBE0 trend (1).
limitations: Single molecule; no general functional-dependence trend asserted.
items.answer_text: PBE gap = 3.5756300000 eV (rounded: 3.5756 eV). PBE0 gap = 5.2964300000 eV (rounded: 5.2964 eV). Signed difference (PBE0 minus PBE) = 1.7208000000 eV (rounded: 1.7208 eV): the PBE0 gap is larger. This is a single-molecule, single-instance comparison; it does not by itself establish a general relationship between PBE and PBE0 gaps across other molecules.

records.scientific_result: Official data provide both energy-level lists; both gaps and their comparison are our calculated result, not a quoted conclusion.
conditions: Both levels computed at the same fixed PBE+vdW geometry (no re-relaxation at PBE0), per the OE62 methodology.
limitations: Single molecule; the direction and size of the PBE-to-PBE0 change is reported only for this instance, not asserted as a general DFT-functional rule.

source_refs.quote: Table 2 column 6 (energies_occ_pbe, unit eV, method PBE+vdW vacuum) description quote: List of eigenvalues of occupied molecular Kohn-Sham orbitals. Given in ascending order, the last value is the HOMO energy.

Table 2 column 14 (energies_unocc_pbe, unit eV, method PBE+vdW vacuum) description quote: List of eigenvalues of virtual (unoccupied) molecular Kohn-Sham orbitals. Given in ascending order, the first value is the LUMO energy. Only virtual states below the vacuum level (i.e. with negative eigenvalue) are listed. If the LUMO energy is positive, only the LUMO energy is listed.

tasks.object_type: two official orbital-energy lists (PBE+vdW, PBE0) at one fixed geometry
tasks.input_scale: 1.187835819 nm maximum all-atom distance in the 57-atom molecule
tasks.reasoning_scale: 1.187835819 nm; the orbital energies are whole-molecule electronic properties of the same 57-atom geometry already used for QNP008, [1,10) nm
tasks.geometry_necessity: The shared geometry anchors both energy sets to one real 1-10 nm molecule; extraction requires the documented ordering convention, not a direct lookup.
tasks.learning_objective: Compare HOMO-LUMO gaps computed at two different DFT functional levels (semi-local PBE+vdW vs hybrid PBE0) for the same real molecule, mirroring the already-accepted QNI006 (MEHLOA) design on a new molecule, without generalizing beyond this single instance.
tasks.selection_rationale: JIMHOC already qualifies for [1,10) nm and is already an active geometry candidate (QNP008); reusing it for its orbital-gap data completes the cell without introducing an unvetted new structure.
tasks.input_plan: The JIMHOC XYZ geometry plus the official PBE+vdW(vacuum) and PBE0(vacuum) occupied/unoccupied energy lists.

items.question: For OE62 molecule JIMHOC (the same geometry already used in QNP008), using the attached geometry and the official PBE+vdW(vacuum) and PBE0(vacuum) orbital-energy lists, identify the HOMO and LUMO at each level and compute both HOMO-LUMO gaps. Report both gaps in eV to four decimal places, state the signed difference (PBE0 gap minus PBE gap), and explain whether this single molecule alone establishes a general relationship between the two functionals.
items.model_input:
The attachment is the JIMHOC XYZ geometry (S0002), 57 atoms. Coordinates are in angstrom (1 nm = 10 angstrom). Atom rows are numbered starting at 1, immediately after the two header lines. This is a single relaxed molecular geometry, not a periodic cell. Occupied orbital energies are listed in ascending order; the HOMO is the last (highest) value in the occupied list. Unoccupied orbital energies are also listed in ascending order; the LUMO is the first (lowest) value in the unoccupied list. The HOMO-LUMO gap is LUMO minus HOMO, in eV.

PBE+vdW(vacuum) occupied energies (eV): -4.196 is the HOMO (last value of the full list). PBE+vdW(vacuum) unoccupied energies (eV): -0.6203700000000001 is the LUMO (first value of the full list). PBE0(vacuum) occupied energies (eV): -5.2578700000000005 is the HOMO (last value). PBE0(vacuum) unoccupied energies (eV): 0.038560000000000004 is the LUMO (first value).

answer_refs.quote: Table 2 column 6 (energies_occ_pbe, unit eV, method PBE+vdW vacuum) description quote: List of eigenvalues of occupied molecular Kohn-Sham orbitals. Given in ascending order, the last value is the HOMO energy.

Table 2 column 14 (energies_unocc_pbe, unit eV, method PBE+vdW vacuum) description quote: List of eigenvalues of virtual (unoccupied) molecular Kohn-Sham orbitals. Given in ascending order, the first value is the LUMO energy. Only virtual states below the vacuum level (i.e. with negative eigenvalue) are listed. If the LUMO energy is positive, only the LUMO energy is listed.

items.rubric: 5 points: PBE gap within 0.0001 eV (1); PBE0 gap within 0.0001 eV (1); correct signed difference within 0.0001 eV (1); correctly states the PBE0 gap is larger (1); explicitly states this single molecule does not establish a general PBE-vs-PBE0 trend (1).
limitations: Single molecule; no general functional-dependence trend asserted.
items.reference_answer: PBE gap = 3.5756300000 eV (rounded: 3.5756 eV). PBE0 gap = 5.2964300000 eV (rounded: 5.2964 eV). Signed difference (PBE0 minus PBE) = 1.7208000000 eV (rounded: 1.7208 eV): the PBE0 gap is larger. This is a single-molecule, single-instance comparison; it does not by itself establish a general relationship between PBE and PBE0 gaps across other molecules.

excerpt.omitted: Full source text / bundle omitted; source locations retained. Prior stage records shown as saved.
